name: The Marsh household — a documented provision dealer, unplaced in the town
head: marsh_silvester

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE PAPER, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The corpus first prints this person at the Democrat of 13 August 1834, column 8, so they are in the town's paper by 1834-08-13 and at no stated time before it; nothing reached says when they came. Last printed 1834-08-13.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1834-08-13 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

basis.note: data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json#arrival_and_origin.tables.arrival_year_of_the_known_layer, restricted to years at or before 1834.

replaceable_by.match: a dated source that says which year this household came to Chicago

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

reason_for_coming.value: A store for the traffic of a town filling up
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as provision dealer, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

basis.note: arrival_fill.trade_reasons.a_store_for_the_traffic — the head's recorded trade is evidence about this household, and the draw it answered is the reason the record will carry until a source states one.

lives_at.note: Not attested. NOTHING IS BEING WITHHELD HERE: no source reached says where this person lived, and 52 households in this dataset were already in that position before this one was written.

works_at.note: Not attested as a structure this project models. The trade is documented; the premises are not one of the committed records.

last_dated_appearance.note: NO SIGHTING, SO THE LEG IS A SOURCE'S SPAN. The card holds no dated reading of this person at or before the scene date; the date here is the far end of what a cited source COVERS, which the role's own note calls the source's bound and not the man's. Read from `roles[] (source_span)` as `1833-11/1835-08`, which reaches 1835-08-31 — a window that covers 1835-07-01 itself, so it pins no last sighting before the day and cannot be read as one. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Last printed 1834-08-13, at the Democrat of 13 August 1834, column 8, and nothing reached either follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. A documented resident whose whereabouts on one day are unknown is `uncertain` here rather than dropped: that is the same distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and it is a finding rather than a gap.

persons.name: Silvester Marsh

occupation.note: THE TRADE IS THE PAPER'S. The corpus reads it as provision dealer, at the Democrat of 13 August 1834, column 8. The residents vocabulary's nearest period-correct word for it is `provision_dealer`, and where the corpus prints more than one trade they are all named here rather than reduced to the one the vocabulary could take.

workplaces.basis: The register matches the printed name to the town card marsh_silvester (action: enrich), so this is the same person the resident layer already holds. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

dated_bounds.list_title: Illinois Public Domain Land Tract Sales Database — the federal land offices' sale registers, indexed by the Illinois State Archives
dated_bounds.locator: purchase 0010791, volume 687 page 261, section 10, T38N R14E
dated_bounds.identity_rule: MARSH SYLVESTER matches Silvester Marsh: the forename names Silvester Marsh of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full.
dated_bounds.note: A DATED APPEARANCE IN A LAND REGISTER, AND NOTHING FURTHER. The Residence column reads UNKNOWN, which places this purchaser nowhere: the register did not record where the purchaser lived. A purchase is a TRANSACTION and not a RESIDENCE, so `here_by` is null: nothing in this register says this person was at Chicago on or before any day. Its only column that speaks to residence reads a county, a state, or UNKNOWN, and never a town. THE IDENTITY IS INFERRED AND THE REGISTER IS NOT. The date, the tract and the purchase number are the register's own, indexed by the Illinois State Archives from the land offices' sale volumes. What no source states is that the purchaser is the person on this card: data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json joins MARSH SYLVESTER to this card on a name, upheld under T-0990, on the ground “forename_agrees”. A bound whose subject is inferred is an inferred bound. No grade moves here and the identity is neither reopened nor hardened.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'SILVESTER MARSH' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the Democrat of 13 August 1834, column 8. The corpus associates the name with Chicago; that is where the paper does business with this person and not a statement about where they slept, and the storefront tickets are the ones that may stand a shop there. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `provision_dealer` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 5 times, as “MARSH SYLVESTER”, “MARSH S”, 1835-06-27 to 1836-06-28: 3 federal land entries — E2SW sec 35 T38N R14E; NW sec 10 T38N R14E; W2SE sec 35 T38N R14E and 2 lots in the platted town — lot 1 of block 3 in the town the register codes CHI (L1BL3CHI, as printed); lot 4 of block 3 in the town the register codes CHI (L4BL3CHI, as printed), 320.00 acres stated in all, for $4590.00 (ls0601, ls0711, ls0712, ls1342, ls1341). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $4190.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: MARSH SYLVESTER matches Silvester Marsh: the forename names Silvester Marsh of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

A TRADE PRINTED IN THE 1843 DIRECTORY, 8 years after the scene, carried here by its crosswalk (T-1254, by tools/derive_resident_roles.py). It is NOT a claim about 1835-07-01 and never becomes one: back-projecting a later volume onto the scene is the defect T-1145 exists to refuse. `place` is the address or place of business the record states in its own column; a firm named only inside the printed line stays in `as_printed` for the business band to rule on.

basis.note: Drawn at 93.2% male, the rate measured on the documented roll's own people whose sex the evidence settles (pooled across every roll: this one settles too few names to measure on its own). data/reconstruction/1835_sex_age_model.json holds the measurement.

replaceable_by.match: a source that records this person's sex, a gendered title on their name, or a forename the project's evidence lets fire

sex_basis.note: A DRAW, NOT A READING. Nothing about this person says which sex they were: T-1303 refused the name and was right to. This value is drawn from the measured male share of the roll the person was named on, seeded by their own id so the draw reproduces - retype 'marsh_silvester:sex_ratio' and the same face comes up. It carries no weight as evidence about this person and it is never promoted. The rate is a ceiling rather than a point reading, because the forename table that settled the rest was built mostly on men's names.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 15 under 20', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('marsh_silvester:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0376), AND THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. Every other record in this dataset argues for a household — a family the sources count, or a trade the town demonstrably needed. This one argues for a PERSON: the Democrat and the American name Silvester Marsh as a provision dealer at Chicago 1 time(s), and this reconstruction did not hold them. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no origin, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets. Reading a family, a house or a quarter of town into this record would be reading something the papers do not say. tools/mint_documented_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. marsh_silvester, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1843 — f1843_e1751 (a single entry); marsh_silvester, Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 — n1844_e1232 (a single entry).

address_later.note: Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 prints this address against this person, in the entry quoted on the card: 'Marsh, Sylvester, 98 Lake st. packing house N Water st (See card'. It is evidence about 1844, written here as 1844's and read back onto no 1835 claim. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. The value is the volume's own line, split by its crosswalk on the entry's punctuation. These volumes set the trade first and its qualifiers after it on the same line, so the split may carry an employer, a market or a corner along with the trade. The printed entry is quoted beside the value for exactly that reason: the split is checkable against it, and neither is read into an 1835 claim.

back_projection.note: REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE RECORD. Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 prints an address against this name in 1844 and this pass will not carry it back to 1835. The directory prints this as a RESIDENCE — its own `res`, `bds`, `house` or Norris's `h` — and this pass positions businesses. Reading a home address as a shop door would be the pass answering a question nobody asked it. The residence half is T-0669. A refusal is written here rather than dropped so that a later run can see the address was read and ruled on, not missed (docs/ADDRESS-BACK-PROJECTION.md, clause 2).

residence_back_projection.note: A LATER HOME ADDRESS, READ BACKWARDS 9 YEARS. The street is not an 1835 reading: Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 printed where this person lived in 1844, and this pass carries it back to the scene date because nothing in the 1835 corpus says where the house stood. What is claimed is the street FACE and nothing narrower — no lot, no roof, no door count, and no corner even where the volume prints one — and the grade is `reconstructed`, this dataset's word for a figure the reconstruction supplies rather than a source. North Water Street stands in 1835 under that name and in that place, and the entry prints it as this person's home. So the placement is the FACE and nothing narrower, and no roof is dealt. A home is carried back on a weaker argument than a shop is: a shopfront is capital sunk into one street's trade and a lodging is a month's rent, which is why this policy claims less than docs/ADDRESS-BACK-PROJECTION.md does from the same volume. The rule is docs/RESIDENCE-BACK-PROJECTION.md and the liberty is L223; a reader who thinks 9 years is too far to carry a house should read the grade as the disagreement being invited.
